cards.explanation: The answer is that they shut it in people's faces. Jesus says, "You shut the kingdom of heaven in men’s faces." They don't walk in themselves, and they don't let in those who wish to enter. Picture someone standing in a doorway, not going through and not stepping aside either. That's a line nobody wants to be stuck behind, friends.

The answer is False. Jesus says, "You yourselves do not enter, nor will you let in those who wish to enter." So they stay outside, and they block the way for others. That's a double lockout, friends. It's like me standing at my oven refusing to bake, and shooing everybody else away from the dough.

The answer is twice as much a son of hell as they are. Jesus says, "…you make him twice as much a son of hell as you are." That's a heavy line, friends, so I'll let it stand just as He said it. They travel land and sea for one convert, and this is what Jesus says that effort produces.

The answer is gold. Jesus quotes their rule: "…if anyone swears by the gold of the temple, he is bound by his oath." In that same rule, they say an oath by the temple means nothing, but an oath by the gold binds you. Jesus calls them "blind guides" for it, friends. Then He asks which is greater.

The answer is that the temple makes the gold sacred. Jesus asks, "Which is greater: the gold, or the temple that makes it sacred?" The gold only counts as sacred because of the temple. So treating the gold as the bigger deal gets it backwards. That's like valuing the sprinkles over the cookie, which I'll admit I've done on a hungry day.

The answer is True. Jesus says, "…he who swears by the altar swears by it and by everything on it." So the gift on the altar isn't some separate thing the oath skips over, friends. It all gets folded into one oath. That's Jesus answering their rule in one sentence.

The answer is throne. Jesus says, "…he who swears by heaven swears by God’s throne and by the One who sits on it." So even swearing by heaven points straight to God, friends. There's no word in that oath that stands apart from Him.

The answer is justice, mercy and faithfulness. Jesus names them: "justice, mercy, and faithfulness." He calls these the weightier matters of the law. Then He says they should have practiced these, "…without neglecting the former." So He's lifting up the heavy things, friends, and not tossing out the small ones.

The answer is False. Jesus says they should practice justice, mercy and faithfulness, "…without neglecting the former." So the tithing of mint, dill and cumin stays, and the weightier things join it. It's an and, not an or, friends. In my bakery I need the timer AND the dough.

The answer is that they fuss over tiny things and miss huge ones. Jesus says, "You strain out a gnat but swallow a camel." A gnat is tiny and a camel is enormous. They're careful about the small thing and they swallow the giant one. Right before this, He says they have disregarded justice, mercy and faithfulness, so I think that's the kind of big thing they miss.

The answer is greed and self-indulgence. Jesus says they clean the outside of the cup and dish, "…but inside they are full of greed and self-indulgence." The outside looks good and the inside tells a different story, friends. Think of a mug that looks spotless until somebody checks the bottom.

The answer is True. Jesus says, "Blind Pharisee! First clean the inside of the cup and dish, so that the outside may become clean as well." Inside first, and then the outside follows, friends. The order is the whole point.

The answer is dead men's bones. The tombs look beautiful on the outside, but inside they're full of "…dead men’s bones and every kind of impurity." It's a heavy picture, friends, so I'll leave it plain. Looking nice outside and being something else inside is exactly what Jesus is pointing at.

The answer is True. Jesus says, "…on the outside you appear to be righteous, but on the inside you are full of hypocrisy and wickedness." So looking righteous and being righteous are two different things, friends. He says it in plain words right after the tomb picture.

The answer is that they're sons of those who murdered the prophets. Jesus says, "So you testify against yourselves that you are the sons of those who murdered the prophets." They had said they wouldn't have been partners with their fathers in shedding the prophets' blood. Jesus says that same saying testifies they are those fathers' sons. The murder of prophets is heavy, friends, so I'll say it straight.

The answer is hell. Jesus asks, "How will you escape the sentence of hell?" That's a heavy question, friends, so I'll leave it just as He said it. Right before it, He calls them "snakes" and a "…brood of vipers!"

The answer is Abel. Jesus says, "…from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Berechiah…" Abel's story is in Genesis 4:8, where his brother Cain killed him. So Jesus reaches from the very first killing in the Bible to Zechariah, who was murdered between the temple and the altar.

The answer is a hen gathering her chicks under her wings. Jesus says, "…how often I have longed to gather your children together, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings…" It's a close, gentle picture, friends. I think it's one of the tenderest lines in the whole chapter.

The answer is False. After saying how often He longed to gather them, Jesus says, "…but you were unwilling!" So the longing is there and the willingness isn't. I think that's the tender, sad part of this verse, friends.

The answer is words of blessing. Jesus says, "…you will not see Me again until you say, ‘Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord.’…" The words begin with "Blessed." So the words Jesus names are words of blessing, friends. And that's the end of this teaching.
